query_builder_contract.normalisation: strings.Fields(lower(trim(raw))); per token keep only a-z, 0-9 and runes >= 128; drop tokens with < 3 runes
query_builder_contract.operators: user cannot inject operators: every kept token becomes +token* (required, prefix); tokens joined with space; BOOLEAN MODE

query_builder_contract.emails_punctuation: punctuation inside a token is deleted and the parts concatenated (ana@x.com -> anaxcom, garcia-lopez -> garcialopez); InnoDB indexes ana / x / com separately, so such concatenated tokens cannot match via FT on MySQL either; the prefix LIKE branch is what finds emails

known_differences: accent folding: InnoDB compares via utf8mb4_general_ci (accent/case-insensitive), PG 'simple' only lowercases -> 'garcia' does not match 'García' on PG

stopwords: InnoDB default stopword list (if innodb_ft_enable_stopword=ON) drops words like 'the','for','with','com','www' from the index; PG 'simple' has none -> a query token that is an InnoDB stopword behaves differently (exact InnoDB behaviour for +stopword* in BOOLEAN MODE to be confirmed with production settings)
tokenisation: PG default parser recognises emails/URLs/hosts as single tokens (ana@x.com) and splits hyphenated words differently; InnoDB splits on non-word characters
token length: InnoDB innodb_ft_min_token_size (default 3) excludes short stored words from the index; PG indexes all lengths (query side already drops <3)
relevance/ordering: not used (ORDER BY is explicit), no difference
